newsitem.title: GERMANY: German area bans gatherings on nuclear waste route.
newsitem.headline: German area bans gatherings on nuclear waste route.

text.p: German regional authorities said on Thursday they would ban gatherings along the route of a shipment of nuclear waste due to arrive next month, as fears mounted that mass protests would disrupt the delivery.

A spokesman for the northern district of Lueneburg said gatherings within 50 metres (150 feet) of the railway tracks and roads where the waste is due to be transported would be banned from March 3 to 7.
The order also bans gatherings in a 500 metre radius around the loading station and around the nuclear waste dump at Gorleben in northern Germany, the destination of the shipment.
The medium-term nuclear storage site at Gorleben, east of Hanover, is a favourite target of the anti-nuclear movement.

Last year local authorities issued a similar ban, but violent protests still took place and more than 19,000 police and border guards joined the biggest security operation in German peacetime history to get a shipment to the plant.
Anti-nuclear activists complained against Lueneburg's latest ban, and the local citizens' group said it infringed their right to demonstrate freely.
The environmentalist group Greenpeace placed notices in newspapers calling for peaceful protests against the shipment, which its spokesman Helmut Hirsch called "unnecessary and dangerous".
Germany's environmentalist Greens have already said they plan to join mass protests when the containers reach the dump.
The latest delivery will include two rail containers from France and four more from German power plants, being moved at the same time to save costs for the required security operation.
